rationale: PINS `decorates` FOR THE DECLARATION-POSITION MACROS AND PINS THE MACRO-CALL NEGATIVE. The contract (`src/ast/types.ts`, Decorates) is DECORATED DECLARATION -> DECORATOR, and Julia's macros are applied to the syntax they wrap, so `@inline function fast` is an application of `inline` to `fast`, not a call. Four shapes are pinned because a rule that only reads the first argument would miss three of them: (1) `Base.@kwdef mutable struct Config` puts the declaration FIRST and the macro is MODULE-QUALIFIED, so the target is the bare `kwdef` the analyzer can read from the macro identifier; (2) `@inline function fast` is the ordinary long form; (3) `@doc "…" function documented` puts a STRING before the declaration, which is why the rule scans the whole `macro_argument_list` rather than child 0; (4) `@inline short(x) = x` is the short form, whose declaration is an assignment whose LEFT side is a call. THE NEGATIVE IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: `@time fast(1)` runs a call and must stay `calls` -> `time` (with `isMacroCall`) and must never become a `decorates` row, because there is no declaration under it. The forbid row pins that absence: an implementation that started calling every macro a decorator would pass all four positive rows and fail this one.

expectRelationships.comment: FIRE (1) — a module-qualified macro applied to a mutable struct. The declaration is first in the argument list.
FIRE (2) — the ordinary long form; the declaration is the macro's only argument.
FIRE (3) — a docstring precedes the declaration, so a reader that only looks at the first argument misses this one.
FIRE (4) — the short form `short(x) = x` is an ASSIGNMENT, not a function_definition; its declaration is the assignment's left-hand call.
NEGATIVE — `@time fast(1)` executes a call; there is no declaration to decorate, so it stays a macro call.
NEGATIVE — the CALL inside the macro argument is a real call to `fast` and is published as one.

forbidRelationships.comment: a macro with no declaration argument is a call, not a decorator
the module qualifier is not the decorator; the macro's own name is
